name: Pulsar
scope: A person with INTERMEDIATE proficiency level in Pulsar as a competency should be able to explain Pulsar’s architecture (brokers, bookies, ZooKeeper/metadata store, producers, consumers, topics, partitions, subscriptions), compare Pulsar to Kafka/RabbitMQ, and choose when to use it. They should configure and use core messaging models and subscription types (exclusive, shared, failover, key_shared), understand delivery semantics (at-most/least-once), acknowledgments, batching, routing, retention, DLQ/retry topics, and deduplication. They can define and evolve schemas (Avro, JSON, Protobuf), manage compatibility, use compression, and design topic/schema strategies. They are comfortable with at least one Pulsar client library (Java, Python, Go), handling producer/consumer configuration, error handling, batching, message properties, and integrating into microservices or pipelines. They understand BookKeeper’s role, ensemble/quorum settings, compaction, retention, and geo-replication basics. They can design multi-tenant namespace/topic hierarchies, partitioning, scaling strategies, and use namespace policies. They can write and deploy Pulsar Functions, configure connectors (JDBC, S3, Kafka, Debezium), and understand connector guarantees and operational settings. They can estimate capacity, tune performance (batching, compression, resource limits), and interpret Pulsar metrics (throughput, backlog, resource usage). They understand authentication, authorization, TLS, and namespace-level governance, and can apply security best practices. They use Pulsar CLI tools (pulsar, pulsar-admin, pulsar-client), basic admin UI, and integrate with CI/CD, Helm, Docker, and infrastructure-as-code. They design and execute functional, integration, and resilience tests (ordering, retries, DLQ, schema evolution), simulate failures, and validate non-functional requirements. They collaborate on Pulsar-based solution design, review messaging patterns, document topic contracts and error handling, communicate with ops/security, and mentor juniors on key concepts and best practices.

{"sections":[{"name":"Core Pulsar Concepts & Architecture","scope_included":"- Understands Pulsar’s high-level purpose and positioning vs other messaging systems (Kafka, RabbitMQ, etc.) and can justify when to use Pulsar.
- Understands Pulsar’s logical architecture: producers, consumers, topics, partitions, subscriptions, brokers, bookies, metadata store (ZooKeeper / etcd / K8s), proxies.
- Explains how Pulsar separates compute (brokers) from storage (BookKeeper) and why this matters for scaling and durability.
- Understands the lifecycle of a message from production to storage to delivery and acknowledgment.
- Knows the difference between non-persistent and persistent topics and can choose appropriately.
- Understands tenants, namespaces, topics, partitions, and subscriptions as the core resource hierarchy.
- Can explain ledgers conceptually in BookKeeper (append-only logs) and how Pulsar uses them for message storage and retention.
- Understands basic broker responsibilities: topic ownership, dispatching, load management, and coordination with BookKeeper.
- Understands key architectural tradeoffs: latency vs throughput, durability vs performance, ordering vs parallelism.
- Has working knowledge of Pulsar’s metadata requirements (e.g., ZooKeeper/metadata store roles: configuration, ownership, coordination).","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Messaging Model, Subscriptions & Delivery Semantics","scope_included":"- Understands Pulsar’s core messaging patterns: pub/sub and streaming semantics.
- Knows and correctly applies subscription types:
  - Exclusive: single consumer, strict ordering.
  - Shared: multiple consumers, load-balanced messages, no global ordering.
  - Failover: active-standby consumers, ordering preserved within active consumer.
  - Key_Shared: per-key ordering with parallel consumption.
- Can choose appropriate subscription type for a given use case (e.g., ordering vs throughput vs fault tolerance).
- Understands delivery semantics: at-most-once, at-least-once, and (where applicable) effectively-once; understands that exact once needs application-level or transactional support.
- Understands acknowledgments: individual vs cumulative ack, negative ack, ack timeout, and redelivery mechanics.
- Can configure consumer receive queue size and flow control to handle backpressure and avoid OOM.
- Knows how batching works (producer-side and broker-side if enabled) and its tradeoffs (latency vs throughput).
- Understands message routing modes: round-robin, key-based, custom routing; can use key-based routing to preserve per-key ordering.
- Knows how message retention, time-to-live (TTL), and backlog management work at topic/namespace level.
- Understands dead-letter topics (DLQ) and retry topics and can design a basic retry + DLQ strategy.
- Knows how message deduplication works conceptually and when to enable it (producer or broker side) to avoid duplicates.
- Understands effects of consumer failures, unacked messages, and redelivery intervals on processing semantics.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Data Modeling, Schemas & Message Format","scope_included":"- Understands Pulsar Schema framework and why schemas matter (compatibility, safety, evolution, tooling).
- Can define and use common schema types: Avro, JSON, Protobuf, primitive types.
- Knows how to declare schemas in client code and via pulsar-admin / REST.
- Understands schema compatibility policies (backward, forward, full, always-compatible, etc.) and selects appropriate policy per use case.
- Can manage schema evolution: adding optional fields, deprecating fields; avoids breaking changes.
- Knows how schema versioning works and implications for consumers/producers.
- Understands the tradeoffs between using schema-managed structured messages vs opaque payloads (e.g., JSON/bytes without schema).
- Can reason about message size limits, compression (LZ4, Zlib, Zstd, Snappy), and their performance/storage tradeoffs.
- Understands when to use key/value schema and how it maps to Key_Shared subscriptions for per-key processing.
- Can design topic and schema strategy aligned to domain boundaries (bounded contexts, services) rather than purely technical partitioning.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Client APIs & Application Integration","scope_included":"- Is comfortable with at least one primary Pulsar client library (e.g., Java, Python, Go) and can:
  - Configure clients (service URL, auth, TLS, timeouts, retries).
  - Create producers and consumers with appropriate configuration.
  - Implement synchronous and asynchronous send/receive patterns.
- Understands consumer patterns:
  - Listener vs explicit receive loops.
  - Blocking vs async receive.
  - Concurrency models (thread pools, async callbacks, reactive style where available).
- Handles common error scenarios in clients: reconnection, timeouts, transient vs permanent errors.
- Can use partitioned topics correctly from clients and understands impact on ordering and throughput.
- Knows how to use message properties/headers (key-value metadata) and when to use them vs payload fields.
- Can implement idempotent or deduplication logic at the application layer when needed (e.g., external IDs, upserts).
- Integrates Pulsar clients into microservices, jobs, and batch/stream processing pipelines.
- Familiar with Pulsar’s transaction API at a conceptual level and can use basic transactional patterns where necessary (e.g., produce-consume within a transaction) when supported in chosen client.
- Understands client-side resource management: connection pooling, closing producers/consumers cleanly, shutdown hooks.
- Can tune key client parameters for reliability and performance: send timeout, max pending messages, message routing, batching settings, receiver queue size.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Persistence, Storage & Reliability","scope_included":"- Understands Pulsar’s durability model and how messages are stored in BookKeeper ledgers.
- Knows core BookKeeper-related configuration concepts at a functional level: ensemble size, write quorum, ack quorum, and how they impact durability and performance (without needing deep internals).
- Understands how replication factor affects data loss risk and can reason about basic failure scenarios (single broker, single bookie, rack/zone failure).
- Can configure basic persistence settings:
  - Managed ledger offload thresholds.
  - Retention by time and size.
  - Compaction vs retention tradeoffs.
- Understands message compaction on compacted topics (e.g., for key/value changelog semantics) and when to use it.
- Has a working mental model of how cursor positions (subscriptions) are persisted and how this affects recovery and failover.
- Understands impact of unacked backlog on storage and can design consumers to keep up or use backpressure / throttling.
- Can set basic namespace-level policies related to persistence (replication clusters, backlog quotas, retention policies).
- Understands how geo-replication works conceptually (replication clusters, replicated namespaces) and when to use it for DR or regional distribution, even if not designing the most complex topologies.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Multi-tenancy, Namespaces, Partitioning & Scaling","scope_included":"- Understands Pulsar’s multi-tenant model: tenants, namespaces, topics and the role each plays in isolation and governance.
- Can design a reasonable namespace and topic hierarchy for an organization or system (by domain, environment, or service).
- Understands partitioned topics and can decide:
  - When partitioning is required.
  - How many partitions to start with.
  - Tradeoffs: ordering vs parallelism vs rebalancing complexity.
- Can adjust partition count over time and understands limitations (e.g., effect on existing consumers and ordering guarantees).
- Familiar with namespace policies that affect scaling:
  - Message and byte rate limits.
  - Backlog quotas.
  - Dispatch rate limits.
- Understands broker load balancing at a conceptual level: bundle splitting/merging, ownership moves, and basic tuning levers.
- Can reason about horizontal scaling strategies: adding brokers/bookies, using separate clusters for different workloads (OLTP vs analytics).
- Has awareness of cross-cluster / geo-replication implications on topic/namespace design (latency, consistency, bandwidth).","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Pulsar Functions & Pulsar IO (Connectors)","scope_included":"- Understands when to use Pulsar Functions vs external stream processing (Flink, Spark, Kafka Streams, custom consumers) for lightweight processing.
- Can write, deploy, and manage simple-to-moderate Pulsar Functions (e.g., filtering, enrichment, routing, simple aggregations).
- Knows function deployment options: in-process, thread, process, or Kubernetes runtime (depending on environment) conceptually.
- Can configure function parallelism, resources (CPU, RAM), and retry settings appropriately.
- Understands stateful vs stateless functions at a basic level and when to avoid complex state in functions.
- Can troubleshoot common issues with functions: failures, logs, misconfiguration, performance bottlenecks.
- Understands Pulsar IO connectors conceptually (sources and sinks) and can:
  - Configure common connectors (e.g., JDBC, Debezium, Elasticsearch, S3, Kafka bridge) using provided configs.
  - Map connector configuration to Pulsar topics and namespaces.
- Can reason about exactly-once/at-least-once expectations for specific connectors and design downstream logic accordingly.
- Understands connector operational concerns: batch sizing, commit intervals, offset management (on source side), and backpressure effects.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Performance, Capacity Planning & Optimization","scope_included":"- Understands common performance levers and how they interact: partitions, producers per topic, batching, compression, message size, and acking strategy.
- Can estimate rough capacity needs from requirements (messages/sec, MB/sec, retention window) to guide topic/partition planning.
- Knows how to tune producers and consumers for typical workloads:
  - Enable/adjust batching and batch size/latency limits.
  - Choose appropriate compression codec.
  - Tweak send timeouts, pending messages, max inflight requests.
- Can identify obvious anti-patterns that hurt performance (e.g., too many tiny topics, overly large messages, synchronous calls in hot paths).
- Understands tradeoffs of large vs small partitions and too many vs too few topics per broker.
- Has basic knowledge of how hardware and environment impact performance (disk throughput, network, latency between brokers and bookies).
- Can use metrics and simple load tests to validate throughput/latency assumptions and adjust design.
- Understands that performance tuning must respect durability and availability requirements; avoids unsafe optimizations (e.g., lowering replication factor blindly).","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Security, Access Control & Governance","scope_included":"- Understands basic security concepts in Pulsar:
  - Authentication (TLS mutual auth, JWT, OAuth2, etc.).
  - Authorization via roles and permissions on tenants/namespaces/topics.
- Can work with security experts/ops to:
  - Configure clients for TLS and auth.
  - Request and validate appropriate permissions.
- Knows which operations map to which permissions (produce, consume, functions, admin operations) and can reason about least privilege for services.
- Understands multi-tenant implications: isolating tenants, namespace-level policies, and impact on governance/compliance.
- Has awareness of encryption:
  - TLS in transit.
  - Basic understanding of end-to-end encryption concepts (even if not fully implementing complex setups alone).
- Can apply governance controls in design: naming conventions, topic ownership, schema approval processes, deprecation strategy.
- Ensures sensitive data handling in messages is aligned with policies (masking, tokenization, avoiding PII where unnecessary).","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Observability, Monitoring & Troubleshooting","scope_included":"- Understands key Pulsar metrics and what they indicate:
  - Per-topic/namespace throughput and latency.
  - Backlog size and growth rate.
  - Message redelivery counts.
  - Broker and bookie resource usage (CPU, memory, disk, network).
- Can interpret consumer lag/backlog and diagnose slow consumers vs under-provisioned brokers.
- Uses logs (broker, function, connector, client) to debug common issues:
  - Authentication/authorization failures.
  - Subscription or cursor errors.
  - Timeouts and disconnects.
- Familiar with integrating Pulsar metrics into systems like Prometheus/Grafana and can define basic dashboards for:
  - Health of clusters.
  - Topic-level utilization.
  - Error and retry rates.
- Uses dead-letter and retry topics as observability tools to inspect problematic messages.
- Can perform basic incident triage on Pulsar-based systems:
  - Differentiate client-side, network, and broker-side issues.
  - Collect relevant metrics and logs.
  - Suggest immediate mitigations (e.g., temporarily reducing traffic, scaling consumers).
- Has basic awareness of distributed tracing for message flows (e.g., OpenTelemetry) and can propagate trace IDs through messages where the stack supports it.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Deployment, Configuration & Cluster Management","scope_included":"- Understands standard deployment patterns for Pulsar:
  - Standalone vs production multi-node clusters.
  - On-prem vs cloud-managed vs Kubernetes-based deployments.
- Can work effectively with ops/platform teams to:
  - Specify requirements (nodes, storage, network) based on expected load.
  - Validate that cluster configuration matches application needs (tenants, namespaces, retention, replication).
- Familiar with main Pulsar configuration areas at a functional level:
  - Broker configuration (e.g., advertised address, authentication/authorization enabling, load balancing toggles).
  - BookKeeper configuration basics (journal/data directories, ensemble/quorum settings; without deep tuning).
  - Namespace and topic policies via pulsar-admin.
- Knows how to use Pulsar tooling for administration:
  - pulsar-admin CLI for tenants, namespaces, topics, subscriptions, functions, connectors.
  - pulsar-client CLI for quick testing of producers/consumers.
- Can perform common operational tasks (possibly under guidance):
  - Create/update/delete tenants, namespaces, topics.
  - Create/alter subscription settings.
  - Scale partitioned topics.
- Understands basic upgrade and compatibility considerations (e.g., rolling upgrades, client compatibility across versions) at a conceptual level.
- Has awareness of multi-cluster and geo-replication deployment topologies, and can reason about which topology fits a given use case, even if not orchestrating full deployment alone.","is_non_core_section":true},{"name":"Tooling, Ecosystem & Integrations","scope_included":"- Is comfortable using Pulsar command-line tools (pulsar, pulsar-admin, pulsar-client) for:
  - Quick functional checks.
  - Inspecting topics, subscriptions, and schemas.
  - Managing functions and connectors.
- Familiar with Pulsar’s web/admin UI (if available) or equivalent platform UI to inspect cluster health and topic metadata.
- Understands common Pulsar ecosystem components and how they fit:
  - Pulsar SQL / Presto / Trino for querying data.
  - Kafka-on-Pulsar (KoP) and AMQP/MQTT protocols at a conceptual level.
  - Common connectors to DBs, object stores, search engines, other message buses.
- Can integrate Pulsar into CI/CD workflows:
  - Basic use of Docker images and/or Helm charts (where applicable) for test/prod.
  - Use of environment-specific configuration for endpoints, auth, and namespaces.
- Has awareness of libraries/frameworks that wrap or build on Pulsar (e.g., Spring Boot support, reactive clients) and can adopt them when appropriate.
- Can leverage infrastructure-as-code (e.g., Terraform, Helm values) for Pulsar resource provisioning in collaboration with platform teams, even if not authoring complex modules alone.","is_non_core_section":true},{"name":"Testing, Quality & Resilience Validation","scope_included":"- Designs tests for Pulsar-based components that cover:
  - Functional correctness (messages are produced/consumed as expected).
  - Ordering and deduplication assumptions per subscription type.
  - Error handling, retries, and DLQ behavior.
- Uses integration testing approaches:
  - Embedded/standalone Pulsar in tests.
  - Testcontainers or equivalent for ephemeral Pulsar clusters.
- Can simulate common failure scenarios in non-prod environments:
  - Consumer crash and restart.
  - Network-like issues (timeouts) via configuration or mocks.
  - Message schema evolution and backward/forward compatibility.
- Validates non-functional aspects:
  - Throughput and latency under projected load.
  - Behavior under backpressure (slow consumers, full backlogs).
- Ensures resilience patterns are implemented and tested:
  - Idempotent processing where required.
  - Correct use of retries vs DLQ.
  - Graceful shutdown of consumers and producers.
- Coordinates with QA/performance teams to define test data volumes and patterns representative of production.","is_non_core_section":true},{"name":"Collaboration, Design Practices & Documentation","scope_included":"- Participates actively in designing Pulsar-based solutions:
  - Contributes to topic/namespace design and naming standards.
  - Helps choose subscription types and processing patterns.
  - Highlights implications of design choices on scalability, resilience, and cost.
- Reviews code and designs for Pulsar integrations from peers, focusing on:
  - Correctness of messaging patterns.
  - Error handling and retry semantics.
  - Resource usage and backpressure handling.
- Documents:
  - Topic contracts (schemas, semantics, retention policies, expected usage patterns).
  - Error-handling and DLQ strategies.
  - Operational runbooks for their services’ usage of Pulsar (what to check when alerts fire, how to restart consumers safely, etc.).
- Communicates effectively with platform/ops and security teams about:
  - Capacity and scaling needs.
  - Access control requirements (roles and permissions).
  - Planned schema changes and migration timelines.
- Helps mentor more junior engineers on Pulsar basics: key concepts, client usage, and avoiding common pitfalls.
- Participates in post-incident reviews involving Pulsar and can explain how messaging behavior contributed to issues and what patterns would prevent recurrence.","is_non_core_section":true}]}
